I've been working this land in Quzhou for fifty years. I know what grows here, what the wells can give, and what my body can still manage. I don't need to experiment at my age — I need a reliable harvest to feed my family and earn some cash.

Cotton is my main system and always has been. It's the crop I understand best, and the market for it still holds. I'll give it the biggest share of my land — around 5.5 mu. I'll use the improved Bt variety I've been planting for years. I know how it behaves in this soil. I'll plough deep before planting the way I always have, apply fertilizer in two rounds, irrigate from the well at flowering and boll formation. Pests are always a problem with cotton — I'll spray maybe seven times through the season, watching for bollworm and aphids like every year.

My other 3.5 mu I plant in wheat come October, then turn it over to maize after the June harvest. That rotation keeps the soil from wearing out. Wheat I do with improved seed — I won't risk food security on untested varieties. Maize I do with hybrid seed because even I can see the yield difference, everybody switched years ago. Rotary till after wheat harvest so I can get maize in fast.

I have a small patch of millet and mungbean — about 1.5 and 1.1 mu. These are for household use and local selling. Low inputs, traditional seed from my own storage. I irrigate millet maybe twice, mungbean fixes its own nitrogen so I go light on that.

I won't push yields too hard. I'm 65. I manage what I can manage without hiring too many hands.
